Anya: FYI onboarding new t5x-large-v1 weights to s3://redwood-models/onboard/t5x-large-v1 — pushed yesterday. Tokenizer seems to split em-dash and newlines inconsistently, producing odd structured outputs in code-gen tests. Need serving config validation + golden prompt regression checks. Who can pick this up?

Devin: I can take config validation. Do we have model config + weights checksum? @ci-bot can you post the conversion artifact if ready?

ci-bot: conversion job finished for t5x-large-v1 -> torchscript. Artifact: gs://redwood-artifacts/conv/1711356789-t5x-large-v1.tar.gz ; sha256: abc123def4567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890

Sam: Tokenizer file is at s3://redwood-models/onboard/t5x-large-v1/tokenizer.json. Quick manual check: tokenizing "print(\"hello\nworld\")" produces an extra <nl> token between parens. I'll drop a short script to reproduce.

Julie: For quality gating, we need a golden prompt set: 20 structured-output prompts + 10 tool-calling scenarios. I'll prepare the prompt list and expected JSON schema. Also want to run function-calling smoke tests (search, calculator) to verify arg parsing.

Matt: I'll add a CI eval job that runs the golden set and compares schemas/metrics (BLEU, exact match for fields). Proposed command:
```
./scripts/run_regression.sh --model s3://redwood-models/onboard/t5x-large-v1/ --prompts eval/golden_prompts.json --schema eval/schemas/tool_output_schema.json
```

Anya: Also note serving config: enable kv_cache: true, batch_size: 8, prefill_threads: 2. Without kv_cache we saw 30-50% token latency regression on long-context code-gen. Recommend canary on Dedicated pool with fallback to hosted smaller variant.

Devin: Got it — I'll open a PR with the config changes and add a validation step to ensure tokenizer files match model vocab size.

Julie: @Matt can you reserve 1 GPU on Dedicated for a 2-hour canary window? :pray: 

Matt: Reserved slot today 15:00-17:00 UTC on Dedicated pool. I'll kick off the regression run and post artifacts + logs here.

Sam: Quick test script to reproduce tokenizer quirk:
```
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
Tok = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
s = 'print("hello\nworld")'
print(Tok.encode(s).tokens)
```

ci-bot: Regression job scheduled: ID #6421. Will post results to #eng-ml when complete.

Anya: Awesome, thanks. I'll also update model-metadata.md with weight location, tokenizer caveats, and the weights SHA so onboarding docs are up-to-date.
